Here you will build an `AtomicSAXSCloud`, select an atomic parameter profile,
and switch displaced solvent and hydration on and off with `AtomicSAXSOptions`.
Then you will compare the saved fits of the connected titin model.

**Keep:** fixed domain coordinates and analytical linker and tails.
**Change:** the atomic and solvent scattering model. The full fits also average
four domain conformations; we will distinguish that from the single-domain
experiment below.

::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
Complete [page 2](titin-coordinate-domains.qmd). You will reuse its parser,
cloud-building pattern, and named terminal references.
:::

## Open the worked example

Run this page from `docs/tutorials` in a repository checkout, using the
[environment from page 1](fit-linked-titin.qmd#prepare-your-environment).
The setup loads the measured curve, saved fit values, and display helpers.
You can start a fresh kernel here; you do not need to run the previous page's fits.

{{< include _titin-setup.qmd >}}

The visible examples below run with this setup. Expand the calculation source
at the end if you want the complete fitting implementation.

## 1. Build an atomic scattering cloud

On page 2, we assigned constant atomic weights ourselves. Now choose a protein
profile with `AtomicSAXSParameterProfile.protein_defaults`. `AtomicSAXSCloud`
adds q-dependent form factors, implicit protein hydrogens, and solvent terms.

Parse model 1 and keep the same terminal references:

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
parse_options = pyseb.StructureParseOptions()
parse_options.model_number = 1
atoms = pyseb.PDBParser().parse_file(
    "data/1TIU-heavy-ensemble.pdb", parse_options)
alpha_carbons = [atom for atom in atoms if atom.atom_name == "CA"]

profile = pyseb.AtomicSAXSParameterProfile.protein_defaults(
    pyseb.AtomicSAXSVolumeModel.Fraser1978)
build_options = pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuildOptions()
build_options.reference_atom_serials = {
    "nterminus": alpha_carbons[0].serial,
    "cterminus": alpha_carbons[-1].serial,
}
build_options.calculate_solvent_accessibility = True
build_options.sasa_probe_radius = 1.4
build_options.sasa_point_count = 960
```
The profile sets the atomic-group parameters. Build options control the
geometry preparation and attachment references. Scattering options control
which contributions are evaluated:

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
options = pyseb.AtomicSAXSOptions()
options.solvent_electron_density = 0.334
options.hydration_model = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationModel.SpatialShell
options.hydration_water_model = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationWaterModel.BondedWater
build_options.hydration_shell_convention = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationShellConvention.Pepsi3

cloud = pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuilder.build(
    atoms, profile, options, build_options)
domain_world = pyseb.World("AtomicDomainTutorial")
_ = domain_world.Add(cloud, "domain")
```
The solvent electron density is in $e\,\mathrm{\AA}^{-3}$. This example uses
the Pepsi 3 spatial-shell convention with bonded-water form factors. The
builder prepares solvent-accessible geometry and shell points; pySEB evaluates
their contributions internally.

## 2. Switch scattering contributions without rebuilding coordinates

Use `get_options` and `set_options` on the cloud to compare three controls:

| Control | `include_excluded_solvent` | `include_hydration` |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Vacuum | `False` | `False` |
| Displaced solvent | `True` | `False` |
| Displaced solvent + hydration | `True` | `True` |

The displaced-solvent term subtracts the scattering of bulk water replaced by
the protein. Hydration adds the excess scattering of the surrounding shell.

```{python}
#| code-fold: false
domain_curves = {}
for label, excluded, hydrated in (
    ("Vacuum", False, False),
    ("Displaced solvent", True, False),
    ("Displaced solvent + hydration", True, True),
):
    scattering = cloud.get_options()
    scattering.include_excluded_solvent = excluded
    scattering.excluded_volume_scale = 1.0
    scattering.include_hydration = hydrated
    scattering.hydration_shell_contrast = 0.0135
    cloud.set_options(scattering)
    domain_curves[label] = np.asarray(domain_world.EvaluateFormFactor(
        "domain", {}, q.tolist()))

figure, axis = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))
for label, values in domain_curves.items():
    axis.plot(q, values, label=label)
axis.set(xlabel=r"$q$ [Å$^{-1}$]", ylabel="Normalized domain P(q)", yscale="log")
axis.legend()
plt.show()
```
You have changed the scattering while retaining the same coordinates and
reference atoms. These are **normalized single-domain curves**, so this plot
compares shape changes; it does not show absolute contrast or a fit to the
whole construct. Normalization removes differences in forward intensity.

**Try it:** change `hydration_shell_contrast` from `0.0135` to `0.0` and rerun
the loop. The last two curves should coincide. Restore `0.0135` afterwards.

## 3. Use the atomic domains in the linked model

An atomic cloud supports the same `World.Add` and `World.Link` interface as
the cloud on page 2. For a single-conformation model, build two independent
clouds and connect `domain1.cterminus` and `domain2.nterminus` to the linker.
The tails remain `GaussianPolymer` subunits.

The saved fits go one step further: they average models **1, 7, 13, and 19**
of the NMR ensemble. This changes domain sampling as well as scattering
physics relative to page 2. Within the atomic controls, every fit uses the
same four conformations, allowing comparison of the solvent settings.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="How pySEB connects ensemble-averaged domains"}
The calculation evaluates each domain's form factor, amplitudes about its two
terminal references, and the phase factor between those references. It averages
each quantity over the four conformations, then supplies them as callbacks to a
`NumericalSubunit`. That subunit has named `nterminus` and `cterminus` references
and can be linked to analytical polymers using the usual graph API.

The quantities come from `EvaluateFormFactor`, `EvaluateFormFactorAmplitude`,
and `EvaluatePhaseFactor`. The two domain copies are selected independently
from the ensemble in the resulting interference terms. Geometry is cached so
fitting the chains does not repeatedly rebuild atom-pair distances. Expand the
complete calculation source below for the callback implementation.
:::

The full comparison includes two displaced-volume profiles, **Fraser1978** and
**Pontius1996**, and a hydration-only diagnostic. Each fit varies the same four
parameters as page 2: linker size, terminal-chain size, scale, and background.
Solvent values stay fixed in this first comparison:

```{python}
#| echo: false
rows = ["| Fixed atomic control | Training reduced chi² | Held-point score |",
        "| --- | ---: | ---: |"]
for name, control in results["controls"].items():
    fit = results["fits"][f"fixed_{name}"]
    rows.append(f"| {control['label']} | {fit['training_reduced_chi2']:.3f} | {fit['held_score']:.3f} |")
display(Markdown("\n".join(rows)))
```
Read each excluded-solvent row against its matching hydrated row. For Fraser,
adding hydration lowers training reduced chi-squared from **55.21 to 43.95**,
and the held-point score from **50.76 to 40.34**. Pontius also improves with
hydration, but both complete models retain large residuals.

The solvent options affect the curve, yet they do not resolve the mismatch
between this hybrid model and the experiment.

```{python}
#| echo: false
compare_curves({
    "Atomic vacuum": curves["fixed_vacuum"],
    "Fraser displaced solvent": curves["fixed_fraser_excluded"],
    "Fraser displaced solvent + hydration": curves["fixed_fraser_complete"],
})
```
## 4. Inspect an atomic realization

The fitted ensemble has no single coordinate realization. These views use two
copies of model 1 and the saved fitted chain sizes. Purple shell markers in
the hydrated view identify the spatial hydration contribution:

```{python}
#| echo: false
show_saved_structure("atomic-displaced-solvent")
show_saved_structure("atomic-hydrated")
```
Use the views to inspect topology and shell geometry. The fitted scattering
averages all four domain conformations, while these pictures show one.

## Optional: fit the solvent options too

Once you understand the fixed controls, you can expose
`excluded_volume_scale` and `hydration_shell_contrast` as optimizer variables.
The saved refinement bounds the volume multiplier to $0.95^3$–$1.05^3$ and
hydration contrast to $-0.027$–$+0.054\;e\,\mathrm{\AA}^{-3}$.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Inspect the saved solvent refinement"}
The optimizer updates cloud options and reevaluates the domain scattering at
each solvent trial. Geometry preparation is reused; amplitudes change.

```{python}
#| echo: false
rows = ["| Complete model | Volume multiplier | Hydration contrast | Training reduced chi² | Held-point score | Accepted improvement? |",
        "| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: |"]
for profile in ("fraser", "pontius"):
    fit = results["fits"][f"refined_{profile}"]
    metrics = results["refined_metrics"][profile]
    print(f"{profile.title()} optimizer: {fit['message']}")
    rows.append(f"| {profile.title()} plus hydration | {fit['x'][4]:.6f} | "
                f"{fit['x'][5]:+.6f} | {fit['training_reduced_chi2']:.3f} | "
                f"{fit['held_score']:.3f} | {'yes' if metrics['accepted'] else 'no'} |")
display(Markdown("\n".join(rows)))
```
Both refinements reduce the scores, but neither meets the screening rule:
convergence, improved held-point score, and no solvent parameter at a bound.
Both reach the evaluation limit and the hydration bound. Fraser training
reduced chi-squared reaches **23.71**, which still leaves a poor fit.

This screening rule is a practical diagnostic, rather than a significance test.
The alternating held points are close to training points and may be correlated.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Atomic and hydration conventions"}
Atomic clouds use Cromer–Mann form factors, standard implicit protein hydrogens,
and Gaussian displaced-solvent terms. Fraser and Pontius select different
atomic-group volume tables; the full FoXS reciprocal excluded-solvent convention
is a separate choice.

The Pepsi 3 spatial hydration shell uses a default 3 Å grid and bonded-water
form factors. Its effective point weights include a reference bulk-density
prefactor; fractional atomic exposure does not directly set those weights.
The hydration implementation was independently validated, but agreement of one
component does not validate the complete titin model. FoXS and Pepsi-SAXS are
optional external validation tools, rather than runtime dependencies.
:::

## Continue

You can now build an atomic cloud and change solvent contributions through
its options. The linked model still assigns domain and chain amplitudes by
residue count. Next, [change their relative scattering weights](titin-relative-weights.qmd)
through the analytical subunits' parameter dictionaries.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Complete calculation source: atomic controls and solvent refinement"}

These are the complete calculation cells used by the sequence generator.
They run in sequence order across the four pages; fitting and export cells
are disabled during website rendering. The short examples above can be run
after this page's setup without regenerating the fits.

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Build the atomic clouds and evaluate the six controls"
ensemble_path = data_directory / "1TIU-heavy-ensemble.pdb"
ensemble_models = (1, 7, 13, 19)
cache_q = np.linspace(0.0, q.max(), 401)

atomic_profiles = {
    "fraser": pyseb.AtomicSAXSParameterProfile.protein_defaults(
        pyseb.AtomicSAXSVolumeModel.Fraser1978
    ),
    "pontius": pyseb.AtomicSAXSParameterProfile.protein_defaults(
        pyseb.AtomicSAXSVolumeModel.Pontius1996
    ),
}


def empty_atomic_cache():
    return {
        "form_factor": [],
        "n_amplitude": [],
        "c_amplitude": [],
        "nc_phase": [],
        "rg2": [],
        "n_sigma2": [],
        "c_sigma2": [],
        "nc_sigma2": [],
    }


parsed_ensemble = {}
for model_number in ensemble_models:
    parse_options = pyseb.StructureParseOptions()
    parse_options.model_number = model_number
    parsed_ensemble[model_number] = pyseb.PDBParser().parse_file(
        str(ensemble_path), parse_options
    )


atomic_sources = {name: [] for name in atomic_profiles}
for profile_name, profile in atomic_profiles.items():
    for model_number, atoms in parsed_ensemble.items():
        alpha_carbons = [atom for atom in atoms if atom.atom_name == "CA"]

        build_options = pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuildOptions()
        build_options.calculate_solvent_accessibility = True
        build_options.sasa_probe_radius = 1.4
        build_options.sasa_point_count = 960
        build_options.reference_atom_serials = {
            "nterminus": alpha_carbons[0].serial,
            "cterminus": alpha_carbons[-1].serial,
        }

        initial_options = pyseb.AtomicSAXSOptions()
        initial_options.solvent_electron_density = 0.334
        initial_options.hydration_model = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationModel.SpatialShell
        initial_options.hydration_water_model = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationWaterModel.BondedWater
        build_options.hydration_shell_convention = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationShellConvention.Pepsi3
        cloud = pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuilder.build(
            atoms, profile, initial_options, build_options
        )
        cloud_world = pyseb.World(
            f"I27{profile_name.title()}Model{model_number}"
        )
        cloud_world.Add(cloud, "domain")
        atomic_sources[profile_name].append((cloud, cloud_world))


def evaluate_atomic_ensemble(
    profile_name,
    q_values,
    include_excluded_solvent,
    excluded_volume_scale,
    include_hydration,
    hydration_shell_contrast,
):
    cache = empty_atomic_cache()
    q_values = np.asarray(q_values, dtype=float)
    q_list = q_values.tolist()

    for cloud, cloud_world in atomic_sources[profile_name]:
        options = cloud.get_options()
        options.solvent_electron_density = 0.334
        options.include_excluded_solvent = include_excluded_solvent
        options.excluded_volume_scale = excluded_volume_scale
        options.include_hydration = include_hydration
        options.hydration_shell_contrast = hydration_shell_contrast
        options.hydration_volume_per_exposed_atom = 30.0
        cloud.set_options(options)

        cache["form_factor"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateFormFactor("domain", {}, q_list)
        )
        cache["n_amplitude"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateFormFactorAmplitude(
                "domain.nterminus", {}, q_list
            )
        )
        cache["c_amplitude"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateFormFactorAmplitude(
                "domain.cterminus", {}, q_list
            )
        )
        cache["nc_phase"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluatePhaseFactor(
                "domain.nterminus", "domain.cterminus", {}, q_list
            )
        )
        cache["rg2"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateRadiusOfGyration2("domain", {})
        )
        cache["n_sigma2"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateSMSDRef2Scat("domain.nterminus", {})
        )
        cache["c_sigma2"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateSMSDRef2Scat("domain.cterminus", {})
        )
        cache["nc_sigma2"].append(
            cloud_world.EvaluateSMSDRef2Ref(
                "domain.nterminus", "domain.cterminus", {}
            )
        )
    return cache


solvent_controls = {
    "vacuum": {
        "label": "vacuum",
        "profile": "fraser",
        "excluded": False,
        "hydration": False,
    },
    "fraser_excluded": {
        "label": "Fraser excluded solvent",
        "profile": "fraser",
        "excluded": True,
        "hydration": False,
    },
    "pontius_excluded": {
        "label": "Pontius excluded solvent",
        "profile": "pontius",
        "excluded": True,
        "hydration": False,
    },
    "hydration_only": {
        "label": "hydration only",
        "profile": "fraser",
        "excluded": False,
        "hydration": True,
    },
    "fraser_complete": {
        "label": "Fraser plus hydration",
        "profile": "fraser",
        "excluded": True,
        "hydration": True,
    },
    "pontius_complete": {
        "label": "Pontius plus hydration",
        "profile": "pontius",
        "excluded": True,
        "hydration": True,
    },
}

atomic_caches = {}
for control_name, control in solvent_controls.items():
    atomic_caches[control_name] = evaluate_atomic_ensemble(
        control["profile"],
        cache_q,
        control["excluded"],
        1.0,
        control["hydration"],
        0.0135,
    )

print(f"NMR conformations retained: {len(ensemble_models)}")
print(
    "Atomic plus shell scatterers per cloud: "
    f"{atomic_sources['fraser'][0][0].scatterer_count()}"
)
```

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
#| code-summary: "Connect ensemble-averaged domain callbacks"
def interpolate_atomic_cache(cache, q_grid=cache_q):
    return {
        "form_factor": CubicSpline(
            q_grid, np.mean(cache["form_factor"], axis=0)
        ),
        "n_amplitude": CubicSpline(
            q_grid, np.mean(cache["n_amplitude"], axis=0)
        ),
        "c_amplitude": CubicSpline(
            q_grid, np.mean(cache["c_amplitude"], axis=0)
        ),
        "nc_phase": CubicSpline(
            q_grid, np.mean(cache["nc_phase"], axis=0)
        ),
        "rg2": np.mean(cache["rg2"]),
        "n_sigma2": np.mean(cache["n_sigma2"]),
        "c_sigma2": np.mean(cache["c_sigma2"]),
        "nc_sigma2": np.mean(cache["nc_sigma2"]),
    }


atomic_ensembles = {
    mode: interpolate_atomic_cache(cache)
    for mode, cache in atomic_caches.items()
}


def ensemble_domain(ensemble):
    domain = pyseb.NumericalSubunit(pyseb.NormalizationMode.Normalized)
    domain.addReferencePoint("nterminus")
    domain.addReferencePoint("cterminus")
    domain.setTotalBeta(domain_beta)
    domain.setFormFactorFunction(
        lambda q_value, parameters: float(
            ensemble["form_factor"](q_value)
        )
    )
    domain.setFormFactorAmplitudeFunction(
        "nterminus",
        lambda q_value, parameters: float(
            ensemble["n_amplitude"](q_value)
        ),
    )
    domain.setFormFactorAmplitudeFunction(
        "cterminus",
        lambda q_value, parameters: float(
            ensemble["c_amplitude"](q_value)
        ),
    )
    domain.setPhaseFactorFunction(
        "nterminus",
        "cterminus",
        lambda q_value, parameters: float(
            ensemble["nc_phase"](q_value)
        ),
    )
    domain.setRadiusOfGyration2Provider(
        lambda parameters: ensemble["rg2"]
    )
    domain.setSigmaMSDRef2ScatProvider(
        "nterminus",
        lambda parameters: ensemble["n_sigma2"],
    )
    domain.setSigmaMSDRef2ScatProvider(
        "cterminus",
        lambda parameters: ensemble["c_sigma2"],
    )
    domain.setSigmaMSDRef2RefProvider(
        "nterminus",
        "cterminus",
        lambda parameters: ensemble["nc_sigma2"],
    )
    domain.ValidateNumerically({})
    return domain


def atomic_titin_world(ensemble, name):
    domain1 = ensemble_domain(ensemble)
    domain2 = ensemble_domain(ensemble)
    world = pyseb.World(name)
    graph = world.Add(domain1, "domain1")
    world.Link(
        "GaussianPolymer", "ntail.end2", "domain1.nterminus"
    )
    world.Link(
        "GaussianPolymer", "linker.end1", "domain1.cterminus"
    )
    world.Link(
        domain2, "domain2.nterminus", "linker.end2"
    )
    world.Link(
        "GaussianPolymer", "ctail.end1", "domain2.cterminus"
    )
    world.Add(graph, "titin")
    return world


atomic_worlds = {
    name: atomic_titin_world(
        ensemble, f"TitinAtomic{name.title()}"
    )
    for (name, ensemble) in atomic_ensembles.items()
}
```

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
def atomic_curve(world, values, q_values):
    linker_rg, tail_rg8, scale, background = values
    parameters = construct_polymer_parameters(linker_rg, tail_rg8)
    form_factor = np.asarray(
        world.EvaluateFormFactor(
            "titin", parameters, q_values.tolist()
        )
    )
    return scale * form_factor + background


def fit_atomic_world(world):
    return least_squares(
        lambda values: (
            atomic_curve(world, values, fit_q) - fit_intensity
        ) / fit_uncertainty,
        x0=[5.0, 5.0, 0.033, 0.0002],
        bounds=(
            [linker_rg_bounds[0], 0.1, 0.0, 0.0],
            [linker_rg_bounds[1], 30.0, 1.0, 0.01],
        ),
        x_scale="jac",
    )


atomic_names = [
    "linker Rg [A]",
    "terminal-chain Rg8 [A]",
    "scale",
    "background",
]
fixed_atomic_fits = {
    name: fit_atomic_world(world)
    for name, world in atomic_worlds.items()
}


def atomic_split_chi2(world, values, number_of_parameters):
    training_residual = (
        atomic_curve(world, values, fit_q) - fit_intensity
    ) / fit_uncertainty
    held_residual = (
        atomic_curve(world, values, held_q) - held_intensity
    ) / held_uncertainty
    return (
        reduced_chi_squared(training_residual, number_of_parameters),
        reduced_chi_squared(held_residual, 0),
    )


fixed_metrics = {}
fixed_rows = [
    "| Fixed atomic control | training reduced chi^2 | held-out mean squared residual |",
    "| --- | ---: | ---: |",
]
for name, control in solvent_controls.items():
    fit = fixed_atomic_fits[name]
    training_chi2, held_chi2 = atomic_split_chi2(
        atomic_worlds[name], fit.x, fit.x.size
    )
    fixed_metrics[name] = (training_chi2, held_chi2)
    fixed_rows.append(
        f"| {control['label']} | {training_chi2:.3f} | {held_chi2:.3f} |"
    )

display(Markdown("\n".join(fixed_rows)))
```

def atomic_visual_world(profile_name, hydrated):
    atoms = parsed_ensemble[1]
    ca = [atom for atom in atoms if atom.atom_name == "CA"]
    build = pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuildOptions()
    build.calculate_solvent_accessibility = True
    build.sasa_probe_radius = 1.4
    build.sasa_point_count = 960
    build.reference_atom_serials = {
        "nterminus": ca[0].serial, "cterminus": ca[-1].serial}
    options = pyseb.AtomicSAXSOptions()
    options.solvent_electron_density = 0.334
    # A dry scene contains atomic groups only; the hydrated scene adds shell points.
    options.hydration_model = (
        pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationModel.SpatialShell if hydrated
        else pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationModel.AtomCentered
    )
    options.hydration_water_model = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationWaterModel.BondedWater
    build.hydration_shell_convention = pyseb.AtomicSAXSHydrationShellConvention.Pepsi3
    options.include_excluded_solvent = True
    options.include_hydration = hydrated
    options.hydration_shell_contrast = 0.0135
    options.hydration_volume_per_exposed_atom = 30.0
    domains = [pyseb.AtomicSAXSCloudBuilder.build(
        atoms, atomic_profiles[profile_name], options, build) for _ in range(2)]
    world = pyseb.World("AtomicVisualization")
    graph = world.Add(domains[0], "domain1")
    world.Link("GaussianPolymer", "ntail.end2", "domain1.nterminus")
    world.Link("GaussianPolymer", "linker.end1", "domain1.cterminus")
    world.Link(domains[1], "domain2.nterminus", "linker.end2")
    world.Link("GaussianPolymer", "ctail.end1", "domain2.cterminus")
    world.Add(graph, "titin")
    return world

for hydrated, control in [(False, "fraser_excluded"), (True, "fraser_complete")]:
    show_structure(atomic_visual_world("fraser", hydrated),
                   construct_polymer_parameters(*fixed_atomic_fits[control].x[:2]),
                   "atomic-hydrated" if hydrated else "atomic-displaced-solvent")

compare_curves({
    solvent_controls[name]["label"]: atomic_curve(
        atomic_worlds[name], fixed_atomic_fits[name].x, q)
    for name in ("vacuum", "fraser_excluded", "fraser_complete")
})

for profile in ("fraser", "pontius"):
    dry = fixed_metrics[f"{profile}_excluded"][1]
    wet = fixed_metrics[f"{profile}_complete"][1]
    print(f"{profile.title()}: hydration changes held-out score "
          f"from {dry:.3f} to {wet:.3f} "
          f"({'improves' if wet < dry else 'does not improve'}).")

```{python}
#| tags: [titin-generation]
#| eval: false
excluded_bounds = (0.95**3, 1.05**3)
hydration_bounds = (-0.027, 0.054)
solvent_world_cache = {"fraser": {}, "pontius": {}}


def solvent_world(profile_name, excluded_scale, hydration_contrast, q_grid):
    q_grid = np.asarray(q_grid, dtype=float)
    cache_key = (
        float(excluded_scale),
        float(hydration_contrast),
        q_grid.size,
        float(q_grid[0]),
        float(q_grid[-1]),
    )
    cached = solvent_world_cache[profile_name].get(cache_key)
    if cached is not None:
        return cached

    evaluation_q = np.unique(np.concatenate(([0.0], q_grid)))
    cache = evaluate_atomic_ensemble(
        profile_name,
        evaluation_q,
        True,
        excluded_scale,
        True,
        hydration_contrast,
    )
    ensemble = interpolate_atomic_cache(cache, evaluation_q)
    world = atomic_titin_world(
        ensemble,
        f"TitinAtomicRefined{profile_name.title()}",
    )
    solvent_world_cache[profile_name][cache_key] = world
    return world


def refined_atomic_curve(profile_name, values, q_values):
    excluded_scale, hydration_contrast = values[4:6]
    world = solvent_world(
        profile_name, excluded_scale, hydration_contrast, q_values
    )
    return atomic_curve(world, values[:4], q_values)


def fit_complete_solvent_model(profile_name):
    fixed = fixed_atomic_fits[f"{profile_name}_complete"]
    return least_squares(
        lambda values: (
            refined_atomic_curve(profile_name, values, fit_q)
            - fit_intensity
        ) / fit_uncertainty,
        x0=np.concatenate((fixed.x, [1.0, 0.0135])),
        bounds=(
            [linker_rg_bounds[0], 0.1, 0.0, 0.0,
             excluded_bounds[0], hydration_bounds[0]],
            [linker_rg_bounds[1], 30.0, 1.0, 0.01,
             excluded_bounds[1], hydration_bounds[1]],
        ),
        x_scale=[5.0, 5.0, 0.03, 0.001, 0.1, 0.02],
        max_nfev=30,
    )


refined_fits = {
    profile_name: fit_complete_solvent_model(profile_name)
    for profile_name in ("fraser", "pontius")
}


def solvent_parameter_at_bound(values):
    tolerances = (1.0e-4, 1.0e-4)
    pairs = (
        (values[4], excluded_bounds),
        (values[5], hydration_bounds),
    )
    return any(
        abs(value - lower) <= tolerance
        or abs(value - upper) <= tolerance
        for ((value, (lower, upper)), tolerance) in zip(pairs, tolerances)
    )


refined_models = {}
refined_metrics = {}
refined_rows = [
    "| Complete model | volume multiplier | hydration contrast | "
    "training reduced chi^2 | held-out mean squared residual | accepted improvement? |",
    "| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | :---: |",
]
for profile_name, fit in refined_fits.items():
    final_world = solvent_world(profile_name, fit.x[4], fit.x[5], q)
    final_curve = atomic_curve(final_world, fit.x[:4], q)
    refined_models[profile_name] = final_curve

    training_residual = (
        final_curve[::2] - fit_intensity
    ) / fit_uncertainty
    held_residual = (
        final_curve[1::2] - held_intensity
    ) / held_uncertainty
    training_chi2 = reduced_chi_squared(training_residual, fit.x.size)
    held_chi2 = reduced_chi_squared(held_residual, 0)
    reached_bound = solvent_parameter_at_bound(fit.x)
    fixed_held = fixed_metrics[f"{profile_name}_complete"][1]
    accepted = fit.success and held_chi2 < fixed_held and not reached_bound
    print(f"{profile_name.title()} optimizer: {fit.message}")
    refined_metrics[profile_name] = {
        "training": training_chi2,
        "held": held_chi2,
        "reached_bound": reached_bound,
        "accepted": accepted,
    }
    refined_rows.append(
        f"| {profile_name.title()} plus hydration | {fit.x[4]:.6f} | "
        f"{fit.x[5]:+.6f} | {training_chi2:.3f} | {held_chi2:.3f} | "
        f"{'yes' if accepted else 'no'} |"
    )

display(Markdown("\n".join(refined_rows)))
```
